location.basis: Mosaic centre between mounds RGR-1 and RGR-2, placed from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) archaeological-site points RGR-1 at 29.29366 N, 76.11439 E and RGR-2 at 29.29132 N, 76.11074 E, and confirmed by the open mound surfaces north and west of the modern village of Rakhigarhi.

main_system_reason: No system: we found no measurable Harappan line.
notes: The Esri imagery is a Vantor Vivid mosaic of 16 December 2024 with real detail to zoom 18 (0.52 m per pixel). Mound RGR-1 north of the village is an open, levelled field with one small rectangular outline of about 25 m that looks like a modern shed or covered trench; RGR-2 west of the village is a broad, gullied mound with a pond, paths and a few modern buildings, and its long straight edges are embankments and plot boundaries. The excavations of 1997-2000 and 2011-2023 are backfilled or roofed, and the modern village covers the eastern mounds. We found no exposed wall, street or drain line, and Rakhigarhi is not measurable from this imagery.
